statement.p: On a sketch of y = \ln\mathopen{}\left(x\right), represent the left Riemann sum with n = 2 approximating \int_{1}^{2}\,\ln\mathopen{}\left(x\right)\,dx. Write out the terms of the sum, but do not evaluate it:
On another sketch, represent the right Riemann sum with n = 2 approximating \int_{1}^{2}\,\ln\mathopen{}\left(x\right)\,dx. Write out the terms of the sum, but do not evaluate it:

Which sum is an overestimate?
the left Riemann sum
the right Riemann sum
neither sum

Which sum is an underestimate?
the right Riemann sum
the left Riemann sum
neither sum

static.solution:
1\le x\le2, which is where the function is drawn with a heavy line.
left sum right sum
Thus we can see that the left Riemann sum is given by \int_{1}^{2}\,\ln\mathopen{}\left(x\right)\,dx \approx 0 + 0.202733 and the right Riemann sum by \int_{1}^{2}\,\ln\mathopen{}\left(x\right)\,dx \approx 0.202733 + 0.346574.
From the sketches we can see that the right Riemann sum is an overestimate and the left Riemann sum an underestimate.
